thread:
violet: Quick sync 1: customers asking for a 'Performance Corridor' product: predictable low-latency slices for critical paths (search/chat). Need packaging decision: tiered lanes vs single premium add-on.
samir: TL;DR: two options - Lanes as named SKUs (Search Lane, Chat Lane) or a generic Premium Lane add-on that can be route-scoped. Tradeoffs: clarity vs flexibility.
paul: Engineering note: route-scoped lanes require tagging and separate scheduling buckets. Increases complexity but gives sales precise promises.
kelly: Sales preference: route-scoped names are easier to sell. Legal prefers generic add-on to avoid many contract SKUs.
finance-bot: Preliminary pricing: Premium Lane base = $2k/mo; Named Lane premium = $2.5k/mo due to sales requests for explicit guarantees.
violet: Risk: many named SKUs multiplies ratecard complexity and customer confusion. Suggest pilot with one named lane (Search) + generic premium for others.
samir: Launch gating: need 2 paying pilots, infra perf tests (p95 under SLA), billing export with lane metadata, sales one-pager.
paul: Implementation sketch: tags -> `tenant:{tid}:lane:{lane_id}`. Enforcement: soft-priority at launch, hard-reservation later.
kelly: Contract ask: if customer moves a route between lanes, charge rule: pro-rate for remaining period and require mapping change ticket.
finance-bot: Action: create SKU IDs: LANE-PRM-01, LANE-SEARCH-01 (pilot discount allowed). Attach to ratecard draft.
violet: On consumption semantics - do we deduct from tenant quota first or lane quota? Proposal: lane quota enforced first, then tenant pool as fallback.
samir: Guardrail: if lane usage >80% for 24h, auto-notify and propose scale-up; if >110% allow fallback to tenant pool with preemption.
kelly: Sales UI: checkbox to mark route for lane during purchase flow. Also need clear invoice line: "Search Lane (monthly)".
paul: Dev tasks: tagging, scheduler hooks, billing meter. Estimate 2 sprints for soft-priority path.
violet: Decision (tentative): pilot both models: 1 named Search Lane pilot + generic Premium Lane SKU. Soft-priority enforcement, lane-first consumption, 80% alert guardrail. Owners: @paul infra, @kelly sales, @samir product. Check-in Fri.
kelly: I'll draft the sales one-pager and sample contract clause by Wed. :thumbsup:
